newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-CLARKE LEADS PARNEVIK, WOODS SHOOTS 64.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CLARKE LEADS PARNEVIK, WOODS SHOOTS 64.

text.p: Overnight leader Darren Clarke held a four-shot lead over Jesper Parnevik halfway through the third round of the British Open on Saturday after Tiger Woods carved Royal Troon up for a 64.
After taking a two-shot lead over American Justin Leonard into the third round, Clarke collected four birdies in a front nine of 32 while Parnevik had four birdies and a bogey for 33.
That left Clarke on 13 under par overall, with Parnevik on nine under.
Leonard and fellow American Fred Couples both parred all of the first nine holes and remained on seven under and five under par.

Woods followed a superb front nine with a fabulous finish as he charged into contention with a seven-under-par round which matched the Royal Troon Open course record of 64 set by Greg Norman in the final round in 1989, when par was 72.
The Masters champion and world number one's 64 was one shot outside the Open record of 63 achieved seven times.

After being tamed by Royal Troon for two days, the 21-year- old American reversed roles and conquered the 7,079-yard course for the first time to vault on to the fringe of contention on three under par.
Clarke was 10 shots clear of him but with the tough back nine of his round remaining.

Woods negotiated the tough back nine in 32, three under par, including an eagle three at the 542-yard 16th with a 15-footer and a spectacular holed chip shot from down a bank for birdie at the short 16th.
His three-iron tee shot there finished down a bank but he bumped his second shot into the side of the bank to kill its pace and watched as it rolled on to the green and curled into the cup.
He said afterwards he had aimed for a spot on the bank three inches from where his ball hit before bouncing on to the green.
Then he saved par from a greenside bunker at the last.
Earlier Woods had made a par four at the 10th, where he had quadruple bogey eight on Friday, but then flirted with disaster at the same 11th hole where he took a triple bogey seven on Thursday.
This time, after driving into gorse and taking two shots to escape, he got away with a bogey five.
He birdied the 12th from five feet.
"The bogey at 11 kept me going because it could have been much worse," he said. "I played the bump and run at the 17th because I prefer it to a lob shot.
"It's up to the leaders how far behind I am at the end of the day. They are in control because the wind is not blowing," he said.
"I can go lower. I had two bogeys today. But I'm hitting my irons very sharp. I just have to eliminate the bogeys."
Woods started out 13 shots behind leader Clarke after rounds of 72 and 74 and quickly took advantage of the perfect scoring conditions he failed to exploit on Friday.
He pitched to two feet for a birdie at the first and rammed in a monster 40-footer at the second.
He reached the long par-five fourth green in two and two-putted but the short fifth cost Woods his only bogey of the front nine when he missed the green and then missed an eight-foot par putt.
Then he almost eagled the long sixth from 15 feet but settled for birdie.
Woods missed from 12 feet at the Postage Stamp eighth, then just missed a 50-foot birdie attempt at nine.
After his par at 10, Woods drove left into thick gorse at the 463-yard 11th. He donned his caddy 'Fluff' Cowan's jacket and ventured into the jungle but advanced his ball into more gorse.
But he put his third shot to the edge of the fairway, almost hit the flag with a 50-yard pitch and holed from four feet to get away with a five.
Stephen Ames of Trinidad shot 66 to finish on four under par, one ahead of Woods and Australian Robert Allenby, who also had 66.
U.S. Open champion Ernie Els could shoot only 69 and was on level par while defending champion Tom Lehman was on five over after a 72.
Britons Colin Montgomerie and three-times champion Nick Faldo shot 69 and 75 respectively, Faldo after two double bogeys on the back nine.
